issues.legal_issue: Testimony cannot be rejected solely because witnesses are relatives of the deceased.
material_facts: The two eyewitnesses were relatives of the deceased and inmates of the house, making their presence at the scene natural.
They were injured eyewitnesses, and their testimony remained unshaken in cross-examination.
The defence relied on family hostility to argue that the witnesses had falsely implicated the accused.
issues.conclusion: The witnesses’ testimony was not liable to be discarded merely because they were relatives; the challenge to its credibility was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: A witness is ordinarily treated as independent unless there is a basis to find that the witness is likely to be tainted. Relationship alone does not require rejection or corroboration of testimony, though the court must assess it carefully and examine whether a foundation exists for alleged false implication. The Court relied on Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab, Guli Chand v. State of Rajasthan, Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras, Masalti v. State of Uttar Pradesh, and State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and witnesses_are_relatives and witnesses_were_naturally_present and testimony_is_cogent_and_credible

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.witnesses_are_relatives: The witnesses who gave the relevant testimony are related to the deceased or other persons involved.
predicates.witnesses_were_naturally_present: The witnesses were present at the scene for a reason consistent with their ordinary circumstances.
predicates.testimony_is_cogent_and_credible: The witnesses’ testimony is coherent and credible after the court assesses it, including in light of cross-examination.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns credible testimony from relatives who were naturally present, their relationship alone does not result in the testimony being rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for nighttime house-trespass cannot stand where the court has made no finding that the offence’s elements were established.
material_facts: The accused was convicted of an offence involving nighttime house-trespass.
The courts below made no finding explaining how the elements of that offence were present.
The accused argued that he had been treated as a trespasser in his own house.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for the nighttime house-trespass offence and its consequential sentence were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A conviction requires findings that establish the ingredients of the offence. The Court applied this requirement to the charge under Section 458 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and set aside the conviction because the courts below had recorded no finding on how its ingredients existed.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.nighttime_house_trespass_conviction: The appellant has been convicted of an offence involving nighttime house-trespass.
predicates.findings_on_offence_elements_are_absent: The court has made no finding explaining how the elements of the charged offence were established.

issues.definition: On a criminal appeal, a nighttime house-trespass conviction is set aside if the court made no findings establishing the offence’s elements.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing injury may be upheld on the unimpeached testimony of injured eyewitnesses.
material_facts: Two prosecution witnesses were injured in the incident and witnessed the assaults.
That evidence supported the conviction for causing injury.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for causing injury was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the conviction under Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, did not require interference in view of the unimpeached evidence of the injured witnesses.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.injured_eyewitnesses_testified: Persons injured in the incident gave eyewitness testimony supporting the charge.
predicates.their_testimony_is_unimpeached: The injured eyewitnesses’ testimony has not been materially discredited.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, a conviction for causing injury is upheld when injured eyewitnesses give testimony that remains unimpeached.

issues.legal_issue: Serious unexplained injuries to an accused do not by themselves require rejection of reliable prosecution evidence, though they may bear on sentencing.
material_facts: The accused had sustained injuries in the incident, and their presence was undisputed.
The injuries were serious and were not explained by the prosecution.
An injured eyewitness acknowledged that a prosecution witness had beaten the accused after the assaults.
The prosecution eyewitnesses’ testimony was otherwise reliable and had not been shaken.
issues.conclusion: The injuries did not warrant disbelieving the reliable prosecution evidence, but their seriousness was relevant to the sentencing assessment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that injuries to an accused do not per se affect the prosecution version when that version is reliable; serious injuries that are not explained assume importance. In this case, the evidence remained credible, while the injuries were considered in assessing sentence.

predicates.criminal_case: The matter is a criminal proceeding.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_is_reliable: The prosecution evidence is otherwise cogent and credible after assessment by the court.
predicates.accused_sustained_serious_unexplained_in: The accused sustained serious injuries in the incident and the prosecution did not explain them.

issues.definition: When reliable prosecution evidence is challenged because the accused sustained serious unexplained injuries, those injuries alone do not require the evidence to be disbelieved.

issues.legal_issue: The death penalty is inappropriate when the circumstances, assessed with full weight given to mitigation, do not make life imprisonment an inadequate alternative.
material_facts: The accused was convicted of murdering three members of his family and was sentenced to death.
The dispute arose after the accused’s father took back land that had been given to the accused for cultivation, and the accused viewed his brother and sister-in-law as responsible.
There had been frequent family quarrels, including a bitter quarrel shortly before the killings.
The evidence indicated an impulsive act rather than planned assaults, with no evidence of diabolic planning.
The accused had been deprived of his livelihood through the loss of the land and sustained serious injuries during the incident.
The Court considered the killings cruel but found the surrounding circumstances relevant to sentence.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions were confirmed, but the death sentence was replaced with imprisonment for life because death was not appropriate in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 and 354(3) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 360 and 361 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, life imprisonment is the ordinary sentence for murder and death requires special reasons. The Court applied the requirement to weigh aggravating and mitigating circumstances, giving full weight to mitigation and imposing death only when life imprisonment is an inadequate alternative and that alternative is foreclosed. It relied on Ediga Anamma v. State of Andhra Pradesh, Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, and Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab.

rule.if: appeal_from_death_sentence and multiple_deaths_occurred and crime_arose_from_family_dispute and repeated_quarrels_indicated_no_planning and offender_sustained_serious_injuries and mitigating_circumstances_remain_significant

predicates.appeal_from_death_sentence: The proceeding is an appeal in which a death sentence is under review.
predicates.multiple_deaths_occurred: The crime resulted in the deaths of multiple victims.
predicates.crime_arose_from_family_dispute: The crime arose from a dispute among family members.
predicates.repeated_quarrels_indicated_no_planning: The history of recurring quarrels supported the view that the crime was impulsive rather than planned.
predicates.offender_sustained_serious_injuries: The offender sustained serious injuries during the incident.
predicates.mitigating_circumstances_remain_signific: After the aggravating circumstances are considered, substantial circumstances in the offender’s favour remain relevant to sentence.

issues.definition: On an appeal from a death sentence, death is replaced with life imprisonment when the crime’s circumstances and significant mitigation do not make life imprisonment an inadequate alternative.
